## Why

Wave A's procurement leg ran a narrow recency pass: USAspending swept a
small keyword list, and the Socrata family (NYC CROL `dg92-zbpx`, Cook
County, WA DES) fetched only a bounded generic `$order`-window with no
keyword filter at all — the register rows themselves are the document
surface, so an unfiltered window is the coverage floor, not a search
surface. I8 §4.2 reviewed the widening as config + a generic
`portal_where` mechanism (ACQ-05): the 17/76-source acquisition term set
drives per-term keyword slices on USAspending (keyword + reviewed
Assistance Listing program numbers + vendor-name recipient search) and
server-side `where` slices on the Socrata registers, with a client-side
vocabulary precision pass underneath the broad `%TERM%` LIKE recall —
and the generic fallback pruned so a record a tighter slice owns never
emits twice.

## What ships

- **Reviewed vocabulary** — `procurement_vocab.toml` →
  `vocab_version = "2026.10.10-p35.9"`: the §4.2 `[terms]` acquisition
  class dictionary (ATE, mobile-forensics, video-analytics, biometric,
  SMM, electronic-monitoring, school-surveillance classes) plus named
  `[acq_keyword_terms]` sets — `usa_spending`, `crol`, `cook_county` —
  and `[portal_where.crol]` / `[portal_where.cook_county]` definitions
  (reviewed field aliases, term set, group size 6/8, `$limit` 500).
  `agenda_content_vocab.toml` gains the vendor/technology literals the
  sets name (Skydio, Brinc, Palantir, counter-UAS, data-broker terms) on
  word boundaries — `brinc` does not land inside `Parsons
  Brinckerhoff`, `clearview` only on the disambiguated literal. No prior
  row or pattern rewritten; Part VIII suppression unchanged.
- **USAspending sweep widening** — `[usaspending_sweep]` joins the
  §4.2 keyword classes, reviewed ALN/CFDA `program_numbers` slices
  (prime assistance rows — a program number IS the listing), and
  vendor-name `recipient_search_text` slices (the recipient-search
  index, sub + prime — a signal the keyword index misses when the
  federal description is generic). Sub-awards stay included; every
  slice carries `slice`, `program_number` / `recipient_search`,
  `acq_keyword_terms`, and finite bounds as provenance.
- **Natural-person recipient drop (P8-6)** — extract drops a payee from
  recipient claims when the record's own business-type literal says
  individual/sole-proprietor, or when the resolution layer's new
  additive `natural_person_signal()` returns the affirmative person
  signal (`sole_proprietor` / `person_shaped`). Ambiguity never drops —
  a two-word company name with no marker keeps its claim. The award row
  stays; `recipient_dropped_count` lands on the slice outcome row; no
  org entity, recipient claim, or grantee assertion is minted for the
  dropped payee.
- **Generic portal `where` support** — a tenant naming a reviewed
  `portal_where` def gets one bounded target per term group, each
  carrying a B00329-shaped OR clause (`upper(<field>) like '%<TERM>%'`
  per field, OR-ed per term, terms OR-ed in the group), `$limit` /
  `$order` preserved, `where_group` + field/term provenance as target
  data — fetch never constructs a query. Unknown `portal_where` names
  fail closed at target generation. Tenants without a def keep the
  plain bounded `rows` target byte-identical.
- **Precision pass + pruned fallback** — `_socrata_where_precise` scans
  the reviewed field text against `agenda_content_vocab.toml`
  (word-boundary, case-insensitive): `PARSONS BRINCKERHOFF INC` drops
  for `brinc`, `CLEARVIEW DATA SYSTEMS` drops for Clearview AI, rows
  with no non-suppressed match drop; `precise_count` / `dropped_count`
  land on the portal index outcome row, honestly zero when empty.
  Fallback pruning is a pure per-record rule — `_socrata_like_owner`
  asks which `where` group's generated clause would have returned the
  row (earliest group wins); the generic `rows` target emits only
  unowned records. No run-level mutable state: `replay()` /
  `run_post_capture()` normalize each capture independently and decide
  identically.
- **Description fan-out** — every populated reviewed `desc_fields`
  alias emits a verbatim `description` claim located to its own field
  (byte-range locator, row/document provenance) — never normalized,
  never inferred; USAspending's populated aliases fan out the same way.
- **Config alignment** — `procurement_portal_tenants.toml`: CROL
  (`procportal_nyc_ny`) carries `portal_where = "crol"` + the reviewed
  `desc_fields`; Cook County + WA DES tenant rows recorded (WA DES stays
  plain — P36.7 re-checks). `live_targets.toml`: seed keyword alignment.
  `ops/cadence.toml`: `task_timeout` rows on the widened procurement
  tasks so a first run is not killed by the default 60m window.
- **Tests** — `test_procurement.py` (sweep composition, recipient-name
  + program-number slice provenance, the natural-person drop with the
  kept ambiguous-company control, `recipient_dropped_count`, description
  fan-out) and `test_procurement_portals.py` (`where` composition and
  group sizing, fail-closed unknown defs, precision false-positive
  drops, honest empty outcomes, fallback ownership/pruning, Cook County
  clause, WA DES plain, description fan-out, shadow + replay zero-diff
  through `run_post_capture`).

#### Test plan

- USAspending: keyword slices name the §4.2 classes; program slices
  carry `program_number` provenance and stay assistance-class;
  recipient slices carry `recipient_search`; sub-awards remain in every
  slice; the named `usa_spending` term set stamps each slice.
- Recipient drop: a sole-proprietor type literal and a person-shaped
  name both drop; `JOHN Q CITIZEN` drops via `natural_person_signal`;
  an ambiguous company name keeps; the notice and slice rows stay;
  `recipient_dropped_count` reports the drop.
- `where` composition: one bounded target per term group, correct
  field-OR/term-OR nesting, doubled-quote escaping, `$limit`/`$order`
  preserved, unknown def → fail closed, non-where tenants untouched.
- Precision: the Brinckerhoff / Clearview-Data-Systems fixtures drop;
  verbatim vendor literals keep; empty slices emit honest zero-count
  outcome rows; Part VIII-suppressed matches never emit claims.
- Fallback ownership: rows matching a `where` group prune from the
  generic window deterministically (earliest group wins); duplicates
  emit one claim set; index rows still record every window's counts.
- Shadow/replay: `shadow_replay` → `changed_count == 0`; `replay` +
  `diff_claim_sets` → canonical-identical over the real
  `run_post_capture` baseline.
- Part VIII: no person/plate predicates, no forbidden tokens in the
  widened rows.
